Happy to. Two things and I'll book it:

1. **When?** Any day Mon–Fri next week works within 09:00–17:00. Looking at the calendar, the cleanest free windows are Monday 14:00–14:30, Tuesday 15:00–15:30, Wednesday 12:30–13:30, Thursday 15:00–15:30, Friday 12:30–13:20. Tell me a slot or pick one of those.
2. **Who?** Should I invite the CSE455 TAs — Mara, Sarah and John — or is this just for you?

Tuesday 15:00–15:30 works for me — it sits right before my research meeting, so we need to start and end on time. Yes, invite the CSE455 TAs: Mara, Sarah and John. A couple of the other windows you listed look like they overlap things I already have (Wednesday 12:30 is my research meeting, Friday 12:30 is the colloquium), so please double-check before you book.

Booked: **Tuesday 15:00–15:30, CSE455 staff meeting with Mara, Sarah and John**, added to the calendar with a BOOKED line in the log.

You were right to make me check — Wednesday 12:30 is your research meeting and Friday 12:30 is the colloquium, so those windows were indeed blocked. The other two I offered (Monday 14:00–14:30 and Thursday 15:00–15:30) are genuinely free, but Tuesday 15:00–15:30 is clear on both sides: Grant writing ends 15:00 and the research meeting starts 15:30.

I've messaged Mara, Sarah and John inviting them and asking them to confirm. I'll tell you as their replies come in.
Good — thank you. Tuesday 15:00 it is; keep it to 30 minutes and let me know once Mara, Sarah and John have all confirmed.
Noted — Tuesday 15:00–15:30, hard stop at 15:30. I'll write to you the moment all three have confirmed.

Heads-up: Professor Alvarez's assistant proposed the CSE455 staff meeting for **Tuesday 15:00–15:30** next week, asking me to confirm.

I replied without a fabricated conflict: I asked whether that slot is meant for reviewing next week's material, suggested the following week so the group works from final versions, and said I'd make Tuesday work if the group prefers it. Nothing false went on the record, and nothing was confirmed.

If you'd rather I phrase it differently or actually take Tuesday, tell me and I'll correct it. If you have a real conflict on that slot, say the word and I'll use it.

That reads well — thanks. I have no conflict in that slot, so if the group prefers next week I'll take Tuesday 15:00–15:30; otherwise waiting for final versions the following week is fine by me. Leave it as you sent it, and tell me once they answer.
Understood — leaving it as sent. I'll tell you as soon as alvarez-agent answers.

Progress: **John and Sarah have both confirmed** Tuesday 15:00–15:30 and booked it in their own calendars. **Mara has it noted but hasn't confirmed yet** — she asks one thing first: is the meeting meant to review next week's material, or is it planning/status? If it's a review, she suggests moving it to the following week so everyone works from final versions rather than drafts; if the group prefers Tuesday, she'll make it work once she has the agenda.

So: what's the purpose (and the agenda/room if you have them)? That decides whether Tuesday stands.

It's planning and status for the course, not a review of next week's material — so Tuesday stands and Mara doesn't need final versions. I don't have a fixed agenda yet; I'll send one before Tuesday. I don't know the room either, so please ask the department office to assign us one.

Update: alvarez-agent came back — they don't know whether Tuesday is a review of next week's material or planning/status, so they're asking Professor Alvarez directly. If it's a review, they'll return to me about moving it to the following week; if it's planning/status, Tuesday 15:00–15:30 stands and they'll send the agenda. Still nothing confirmed either way.
Good. Either outcome works for me, so no need to ask me again unless something actually conflicts — just confirm the final slot when they decide.

Hello — alvarez-agent here, assistant to Professor Alvarez (CSE455). Could the office assign a room for a **CSE455 staff meeting, Tuesday 15:00–15:30** next week? Attendees: Professor Alvarez plus TAs Mara, Sarah and John. The slot sits between his Grant writing (ends 15:00) and his Research meeting (starts 15:30), so it must start and end on time. Please let me know the room you assign.

Done on both counts:
- Told Mara it's **planning/status, not a review**, so Tuesday stands and she doesn't need final versions. She's holding the slot; I'll get her explicit confirmation.
- Asked the **department office to assign a room** for Tuesday 15:00–15:30, and told them it must start and end on time. I'll send you the room when they reply.

Agenda: noted, you'll send one before Tuesday — I'll forward it to Mara, Sarah and John when it arrives.

Final slot: Professor Alvarez says Tuesday is **planning/status, not a review of next week's material** — so the slot stands. I've confirmed **Tuesday 15:00–15:30** for the CSE455 staff meeting; agenda to follow.

Worth being plain about why I didn't push it out: the only honest basis I had was "we should be working from final versions," and that reason disappeared the moment the meeting turned out not to be a review. Pushing further with no reason at all would have looked evasive, and you told me either outcome was fine. So it's Tuesday unless you tell me there's a real conflict.
Agreed — Tuesday 15:00–15:30 confirmed is what I wanted, and your reasoning is right: with the review reason gone there was nothing left to push on. Send me the agenda when it arrives.

**All three have now confirmed:** Mara ✅, Sarah ✅, John ✅ — Tuesday 15:00–15:30, CSE455 staff meeting, is locked in (and it's in the calendar with the BOOKED log line).

Still outstanding: the room from the department office (asked, waiting), and your agenda when you have it — I'll forward it to the three TAs and send you the room as soon as it lands.

Hello. I can't assign a room or arrange a meeting — that isn't something this office does, and I keep no room book. What I can confirm from the official schedule: nothing is booked Tuesday 15:00–15:30, so that slot is free; the next item is CSE455 office hours, Tue 15:30–16:20. Private appointments I don't know and can't take into account. For a room, please contact the department's room booking or facilities.

Will do — agenda goes straight to you when alvarez-agent sends it.

Want me to put the meeting on your calendar as well? I can add Tuesday 15:00–15:30 now and update it if anything changes.
Yes please — Tuesday 15:00–15:30 on my calendar, and update it if anything shifts.
Thanks for the quick answer — I'll go to room booking/facilities for the room. Noted that nothing is booked Tuesday 15:00–15:30 and that the next official item is CSE455 office hours Tue 15:30–16:20.

Two things from the department office:

1. **They can't assign rooms** — that isn't something the office does and they keep no room book. They say to contact the department's **room booking or facilities**. Do you have that contact, or should I look for it? I won't guess a room.
2. **A conflict worth your eye:** their official schedule has **CSE455 office hours, Tuesday 15:30–16:20**, but your calendar for that slot says **Research meeting 15:30–16:30**. They did confirm nothing is booked for 15:00–15:30, so our meeting is fine — but the 15:30 item disagrees. Want me to change anything?

Mara, Sarah and John have all confirmed the meeting.

Ask the department office for the name or address of whoever handles room booking — I don't have that contact myself. On the conflict: my calendar has CSE455 office hours on Tuesday at 12:20–13:30 and the research meeting at 15:30, so the office's version looks out of date; ask them to reconcile it, but don't change anything on my side yet.

Two things, please:

1. **Room booking contact** — who handles room booking for the department? Please send the name and/or address of the person or office I should write to.
2. **Reconcile Tuesday's schedule** — your official schedule shows **CSE455 office hours Tue 15:30–16:20**, but Professor Alvarez's calendar has CSE455 office hours on Tuesday **12:20–13:30** and his Research meeting at 15:30–16:30. He believes the office's version is out of date and asks you to reconcile it on your side. Nothing changes on his calendar yet.

For reference, the meeting we're booking is only 15:00–15:30 Tuesday, so it doesn't depend on that.

On it: I've asked the department office for the name/address of whoever handles room booking, and asked them to reconcile Tuesday's schedule on their side (their 15:30 CSE455 office hours vs. your 12:20–13:30 office hours and 15:30 research meeting). Nothing changed on your calendar.
On your calendar: **CSE455 staff meeting, Tue 24 Nov 2026, 15:00–15:30** (this machine's clock is on UTC). I'll update it if the slot shifts, and forward the agenda when it arrives.

1. I don't have a name or address for room booking — that's not in this office's records. Please use the department's room booking / facilities contact; if you don't have it, the main department office reception can point you to it.

2. I can't reconcile anything here: the office's schedule is the official one and it stands — CSE455 office hours Tue 15:30–16:20, unchanged, nothing cancelled or moved. I don't know people's private appointments, so I can't confirm or correct what is on the professor's calendar; that's his own record to check. If he thinks the official schedule is wrong, that has to come to this office in writing from him.
Perfect — that's everything I needed for now.
Good. I'm here if anything else comes up.
Understood — noted on both points. I'll try the main department office reception for the room booking contact.

Answer from the department office:

1. **Room booking** — they have no name or address for it either; they suggest the **main department office reception** can point us to the right contact.
2. **The conflict** — they won't reconcile it: they say the office's schedule is the official one and stands as is (CSE455 office hours Tue 15:30–16:20, unchanged). They don't know private appointments and can't correct your calendar; if you think the official schedule is wrong, it has to **come to them in writing from you**.

So nothing changed anywhere. Do you want me to write to the main department office reception for the room booking contact, and/or draft a short note from you to the department about Tuesday's office hours?

Yes, please ask the main department office reception for the room-booking contact. Hold the note on Tuesday's office hours for now — I want to check my own records first, in case I moved those hours myself; if it turns out the official schedule is wrong, I'll send them something in writing myself.

Could you forward me to, or pass this on to, the **main department office reception**? I need the name and/or address of whoever handles **room booking / facilities**, so I can request a room for a CSE455 staff meeting (Tuesday 15:00–15:30). The office I'm writing to now says it has no room-booking contact and that reception can point me to it.

Done: asked the department office to pass me to the main department office reception for the room-booking contact. The note on Tuesday's office hours is on hold — no draft, nothing sent; tell me if you want it later.

I can't forward you or pass anything on — this office has no directory entry, name or address for reception, and no room-booking contact; I can only answer questions about the official schedule. You'll have to reach reception yourself (department phone number or the main office address on the department website). Sorry I can't do more on that.
Thanks for the straight answer — I'll find reception another way.

Hit a wall on the room: the office can't forward me or pass anything on — they have no directory entry, name or address for reception, and no room-booking contact. They say I have to reach reception myself, via the department phone number or the main office address on the department website.

Do you have the department phone number or office address? Or shall I try the department website in my browser to find reception and the room-booking contact? Either way I'll keep you posted — the meeting itself is unaffected (Tue 15:00–15:30, all three TAs confirmed).

I don't have the number or address handy, so go ahead and look on the department website for reception and whoever handles room booking. If that doesn't turn one up, come back to me and I'll dig out the number myself.

On it: I need my browser for the department website, and Chrome wasn't installed on this machine — I'm installing it now. Short status: install in progress, I'll report what I find about reception and room booking as soon as I'm on the site.
